blurb: Four Mac minis from 2011, a switch, and a laptop to drive them. One host is provisioned so far; the rest are hardware waiting for an OS.

hosts.role: room monitor — USB webcam, streams rather than records
RTSP source over Wi-Fi, recorded on a mini

network.topology: gw-1 is the uplink and the only Wi-Fi. sw-1 hangs off it, and the minis and the monitor Pi go to sw-1 over 1000BASE-T; sessions leave air-1 and reach the minis by SSH. The cameras take no switch port — they have no Ethernet, so they join gw-1 over Wi-Fi like air-1 does.
network.addressing: gw-1 hands every mini a fixed address by DHCP reservation, keyed to its MAC, so a reinstall comes back on the address it left on — one source of truth, and nothing to configure on the host. The last digit of an address is the number of the mini it belongs to.
network.disclosure: Addresses, hostnames and key material are not published. Neither is the router's model: an unmanaged switch has no address and no firmware to attack, but a router has both.

services.name: Camera recording
services.note: A mini pulls RTSP from both cameras and records continuously to local disk. Only events leave the house — two 2K streams uploaded around the clock would be terabytes a month, and the off-site copy exists for the case where the recorder itself is gone. The cameras offer RTSP in their app; nobody has yet pointed ffprobe at one and got a stream back, so that is the first thing this plan has to survive.

house_rules: One agent session per host — that ratio is the point of the cluster, not a limitation of it.
Mid-2011 thermals were designed for open air, so the minis sit side by side and are never stacked.
A 288 Wh LiFePO4 station backs gw-1, sw-1 and pi-1, so the network and the monitor outlive a power cut. It does not back the minis: four of them under load would empty it inside an hour.
Nothing here is reachable from outside the LAN, and no port is forwarded to reach it.
